title: Resolve a Conflict During Rebase
objective: Rebase feature/fast onto main and reconcile two changes to settings.txt.
description: The feature branch enables fast mode while main introduces a safety rule. Rebase the feature branch onto main, resolve the conflict so the final mode is safe-fast, and continue the rebase.

lesson.principle: Rebase replays a feature commit on top of main. When a replay conflicts, resolve and stage the file before continuing.
lesson.question: After setting settings.txt to the intended mode and staging it, which command resumes the paused rebase?
lesson.explanation: git rebase --continue resumes the paused commit replay. The final branch should have a linear history based on main.
pitfalls: Running git commit instead of continuing the paused rebase.
Keeping only fast mode and dropping main's safety rule.

hints: Switch to feature/fast, then run git rebase main. Git pauses when settings.txt conflicts.
Edit settings.txt to contain mode=safe-fast, then run git add settings.txt.
Run git rebase --continue. If Git opens an editor, keep the commit message and save it. Then run git-conflict-lab check.
